title: Modality-aware Kernel Prober and Stability Simulation for FlashAttention v2/v3 Integration
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Build a modality-aware prober plus a stability simulation harness to reduce regressions when integrating FlashAttention v2/v3 variants into the serving runtime. The prober will exercise kernels under controlled prefill/decode schedules, synthetic modality slices (short chat turns, long context docs, code-like tokens), and quantization/precision combos. The simulation harness will replay recorded traces plus synthetic load patterns to estimate probability of kernel-instability (OOMs, incorrect outputs, large latency spikes) and surface input-shape/sequence-length regions that drive regressions.

Why this ticket: We've seen intermittent latency jitter and rare correctness deltas during v3 rollout on mixed workloads. Existing kernel-probers are shape-agnostic and primarily measure microbenchmarks. This work aims to (1) attribute instability to specific modality/shape/precision combinations, (2) produce deterministic repro cases, and (3) provide signal for runtime routing policies (prefer v2 for code-heavy long-context requests, prefer v3 for conversational short-context requests, etc.).
acceptance_criteria:
1) A prober binary that runs a configurable matrix: model variant, kernel impl (v2/v3/quant), prefill length, decode length, batch size, and token distribution seed.
2) Simulation harness that can replay a day's production trace (sampled anonymized) plus synthetic modality slices and produce per-kernel risk scores (OOM rate, latency tail delta, token-regression count).
3) Repro artifact generator: given a high-risk cell, output a minimal seed and invocation script that reproduces the failure on a dev GPU node.
4) Dashboard tile in Console showing top-10 risky (model,kernel,shape) tuples and recent regression alerts.
5) Integration tests that run the prober nightly and gate canary rollouts if risk exceeds thresholds.
6) Documentation and runbook for on-call to triage simulator findings.
updates:
2026-02-25 - Aisha Patel: Created ticket after postmortem showed two v3 rollouts with intermittent 95p latency spikes on code-generation workloads. Filed as part of runtime-stability initiative.

2026-03-02 - Marcus Nguyen: Initial spike matrix and proto prober implemented. Can run combinations of prefill/decode lengths and record latency + correctness snapshots. Early findings: code-like token distributions with prefill >1024 and batch size 2 increase 95p by ~18% for v3 on A100-80GB. Linked PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1892 (proto prober).

2026-03-05 - Design review with Sofia Ramirez (UX): Discussed dashboard requirements. Decided to present top-risk tuples and allow one-click repro export. Follow-up: add retention controls for probe telemetry to limit PII exposure. Confluence spec: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/Modality+Prober+Spec

2026-03-08 - Marcus Nguyen: Built deterministic repro generator that trims the trace to ~8-20 tokens around the divergence seed and pins PRNG. Reproducer validated on dev cluster; created artifact: gs://redwood-artifacts/probers/ENG-447711/repro-2026-03-08.tar.gz

2026-03-10 - Aisha Patel: Ran simulation on sampled production traces (7 days, 1% sample anonymized). Results: v3 shows regression hotspots for sequences with alternating short/long segments (chat interleaved with pasted documents). Proposed mitigation: runtime routing rule to prefer conservative v2 kernel for sessions flagged as 'mixed-context' until prober risk drops.

2026-03-12 - Marcus Nguyen: Implemented nightly job to run prober matrix across representative models (gpt-like-std, code-optimized, long-context-2k). Nightly results pushed to internal S3 and a generated JSON risk report. Working on hooking the risk report into Console via runtime-1.21 observability endpoint.

Next steps: (1) finalize risk thresholds with SRE and Product, (2) add canary gating that rejects v3 rollout for a model if nightly risk > 0.05 OOMs per 10k tokens, (3) expand synthetic modalities to include multilingual tokenizers and micro-batched streaming patterns.
